inputs.description: CTable::remove_rows() over 12 index sets on a compressed table deliberately built so std::map order differs from insertion order for both the rows and two of the four rows' TimedCounters, plus 10 more on a 4-input/30-row table whose index sets contain elements >= 8 (so a Python set's own iteration order is not ascending there); lazy_random_selector draw SEQUENCES for 5 (u, seed, n) triples; subsampleCTable() for 10 (ratio, seed) pairs, 8 more at ratios where the binary32 narrowing of the `float ratio` parameter changes nremove, and 10 on the 30-row table; rank_feature_sets() plus select_top_feature_sets() for 33 hand-built feature_set_pops carrying deliberate ties (equal scores, duplicated sets, and the fully symmetric 5-input majority table where every same-size feature set has identical mutual information), across jaccard/mi, four diversity_interaction values and several n_demes; and feature_selector::mi() at full double precision for 22 (table, fs_l, fs_r, diversity_interaction) cases -- most on fs_mi_skewed.csv, which is NOT a full truth-table enumeration and therefore has irrational mutual informations where the other tables have whole numbers of bits; and build_fs_ctable()'s by-TIME subsampling branch for 13 cases, three of them on a table with no timestamp column at all (where classic removes nothing); and feature_selector::operator()() end to end with diversity_pressure > 0 and/or subsampling_ratio < 1. Seeds are set with randGen().seed(...) immediately before each drawing call. NOT captured: the 'hc' algorithm, the only one whose feature_set_pop can exceed one entry -- classic's own 'hc' feature-selection path segfaults unconditionally (measured again here, rc 139; see tools/cpp_probe/fs_standalone_probe.cc).
